items: Fundamental Rights are justiciable and enforceable via Supreme Court (Article 32) and High Courts (Article 226).
The Right to Property was converted into a legal right under Article 300-A in Part XII by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.
Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution of India from Articles 12 to 35.
Part III of the Indian Constitution is widely described as the Magna Carta of India.
Fundamental Rights are justiciable, meaning they are directly enforceable by the courts.
These rights are not absolute but qualified, meaning the state can impose reasonable restrictions.
The Right to Property was deleted from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.
